key_insight: WorldCache replaces naive static reuse of cached features with a content-aware, spatially adaptive caching strategy that updates and aligns intermediate activations across denoising steps, substantially reducing ghosting and motion artifacts while accelerating Diffusion Transformer video world models.
problem_solved: Existing training-free feature caching for DiTs assumes cached features remain valid as static snapshots (Zero-Order Hold), which causes ghosting, blur, and motion inconsistency in generated videos and limits safe speedups during inference.
method: Detect and score cacheable feature regions based on content stability and motion cues rather than assuming global invariance.
Adaptively update cached activations with spatially-varying alignment/warp and uncertainty-weighted blending across denoising steps to avoid ghosting.
Integrate the cache as a training-free module inside DiTs to reduce repeated computation of spatio-temporal attention and sequential denoising without retraining the model.
impact: Delivers substantial inference speedups for high-fidelity video world models while preserving visual quality, enabling more practical real-time or long-horizon applications in robotics, simulation, and content generation.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: Zero-Order Hold (ghosted frame) vs WorldCache (clean frame) to illustrate artifact reduction.
Pipeline flowchart: feature extraction → cache scoring → alignment/warp → blend & reuse → denoising steps.
Bar chart: latency or FLOPs reduction vs perceptual quality (e.g., FVD/SSIM) showing favorable tradeoff.
Icons: clock for latency, memory chip for cache, motion arrows for alignment, film strip for video/world model.
paper_title: WorldCache: Content-Aware Caching for Accelerated Video World Models
paper_authors: Umair Nawaz, Ahmed Heakl, Ufaq Khan, Abdelrahman Shaker, Salman Khan
